messages:
Priya (SE): Hey team — PSC (private-sector client) needs a short POC for our Private deployment. key asks: static egress IP for firewall allowlist, option to use AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering, and confirmation on which ports/protocols need to be opened. They also asked how this impacts monthly cost.
Jason (AE): High-level ask noted. Customer is in finance org, SOC2 required. They want a runbook we can hand to their network team. Pricing note: they will expect an estimate for inter-region data >100TB/month.
Rob (NetOps): Quick clarifying q: do they need inbound connectivity from their VPC to our control plane, or just outbound from their private deploy to our region endpoints?
Priya (SE): Outbound only from their on-prem/VPC to our Private control plane + inference nodes. They want the option to host inference in their VPC (Private deploy) where we install agents, but control plane remains managed.
Elena (Solutions Eng): For that pattern we typically recommend PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint) to the control plane to avoid customer NAT traversal. Peering is possible but has drawbacks for cross-account routing and we can't easily expose a single egress IP over peering.
Rob (NetOps): If customer insists on a single static egress IP for allowing return traffic through their firewalls, options: 1) route traffic via a customer-managed NAT/proxy with static Elastic IP; 2) use our egress-NAT appliance in their VPC (if they permit) which has a fixed EIP; 3) preserve source IP via TP (hard). Which of those can we support for Private deploy?
Priya (SE): We can support option 1 (preferred) and 2 (requires install). Option 1: they route outbound to their proxy -> interface endpoint -> control plane. Option 2: we run a small egress appliance (container/VM) in their VPC that we manage; that gets a static EIP.
Jason (AE): Pricing callout: PrivateLink incurs per-hour endpoint + per-GB data processing costs on AWS. If they push 100TB/month, the endpoint and data costs could be material. Need an back-of-envelope.
Elena (Solutions Eng): I'll ballpark: Interface Endpoint hourly ~ $0.01-0.02 * 720 ~ $7-14/month per AZ + $0.01-0.06/GB processed depending on region. I'll put numbers in the handoff doc.
Rob (NetOps): Firewall rules — minimal set to open from customer -> our control plane:
```
- TCP 443 (HTTPS) outbound to control-plane interface endpoint FQNs
- TCP 443 outbound to inference node IPs if using direct agent -> runtime (if we deploy agent in customer VPC)
- Optional: TCP 22 only if they want us to ssh (not recommended)
```
Also, for SNI/TLS inspection customers: if they do TLS inspect we need them to allow passthrough for our control-plane cert chains else mTLS will fail.
Priya (SE): They asked for a sample security questionnaire snippet: we should confirm data residency, KMS key usage, audit logs retention, and whether logs cross-account. I can draft.
Jason (AE): Also banner for the exec: "Will not store customer PII in control plane logs by default" — they will press on that.
Elena (Solutions Eng): Network runbook checklist (draft):
- Create Interface Endpoint (redwood-controlplane.<region>.vpce) in the customer's account (or we provide AWS account details for cross-account endpoint)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to vpce endpoints FQDNs
- If static egress IP required: configure NAT Gateway or proxy with Elastic IP and reference that in firewall allowlist
- Security: allowlist our management cert CA if performing TLS inspection
- Monitoring: open ICMP only for troubleshooting (optional)

Rob (NetOps): Sample SG snippet for customer (paste into their IaC):
```json
{"Type":"AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup","Properties":{"GroupDescription":"Allow outbound to Redwood PrivateLink","SecurityGroupEgress":[{"IpProtocol":"tcp","FromPort":443,"ToPort":443,"CidrIp":"0.0.0.0/0"}]}}
```
(They will likely tighten to specific vpce IP ranges once we provide them.)
Priya (SE): Action items: Elena — draft runbook + cost estimate. Rob — finalize firewall snippet and EIP workflow. Jason — collect customer security questionnaire highlights. I'll coordinate a 30-min handoff with customer network team tomorrow.
Elena (Solutions Eng): I'll drop the doc in the sales handoff repo and ping here when ready. ETA 6 hours.
network-bot: Created ticket INF-4521 for "PSC POC PrivateLink + static-egress handoff" and assigned to @Elena and @Rob.
Jason (AE): One more thing — customer asked about latency impact if we use PrivateLink vs peering. Elena, can you add a latency/throughput note?
Elena (Solutions Eng): Yes — PrivateLink adds ~1-5ms typical for same region; peering is slightly lower but peering complicates multi-account routing. I'll add perf numbers and a small diagram.
Rob (NetOps): If they want a guaranteed egress IP from our side (we would NAT egress traffic through our fleet), that's an enterprise feature and requires a reserved capacity contract. Flagging to Jason for procurement.
Jason (AE): Noted — I'll surface reserved capacity pricing if they want provider-managed static egress.
Priya (SE): Great. I'll schedule the customer handoff after Elena shares the doc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Elena (Solutions Eng): Putting checklist + diagram + rough pricing into the repo link: https://internal.redwood/sales/handoffs/psc-poc (will update).
network-bot: Updated ticket INF-4521 with attachments: runbook-draft.pdf, sg-snippet.json.
Jason (AE): Keeping this thread pinned for the customer meeting.
Priya (SE): End state we need before handoff: runbook + one-page pricing summary + customer firewall snippet with EIP (or confirmation they will provide EIP).
Rob (NetOps): Agree. I'll also include quick test steps: curl to control plane FQDN, verify TLS chain, and verify outbound IP via https://ifconfig.me.
Priya (SE): Perfect — I'll close once we have those three items.
